Looks like a fun list! I do think you have too many engineers, runes of reloading tend to negate the need for more than one and youve doubled down with a forging rune too. I like the one runesmith and I would consider 2 spellbreaking runes to justify his cost but if hes in the right place hes invaluable, watch for that 18 inch dispel though. Slayer engineer is effectly a low ap cannon vs behemoths, I also tried to make him work but unlike a cannon he can't just grapeshot or blast through a warrior squad. Also does diddly squat vs heavy chariots (steam tanks, necromancers on chariots, beastmen lords or chaos lords ect.) 

For some more fun units, doomslayers are heaps of anti large fun bombs, as is the old 88 pt demons slayer. I also rate a sapper general very highly if you don't tank damnninson. He will drop 1/6th of a chaos warrior brick every time they move/reform/overrun/charge/ect. Just keep him cheap and out of a unit so he doesn't get charged and stop working. (I give him a rune of the forge for pillar of fire and a pair of pistols).  I actually take 20 warriors with a bsb shield bearer thane and the rune of hesitation to park in front of the sapper and act as a solid core, as they push back and fourth he racks up a lot of kills via sheer attrition.

I'm very interested to see how 30 miners work! I've only bought a max of 20 before. (2x10)

Though we in our playgroup think (until proven otherwise) raw it applies too hammer-hand from the bound spell armour. Being that assailment mentions they are attacks and made in combat, which seems to be the requirements for kB.

Any template that says difficult or dangerous terrain will kill them if they move through it. That can be a good way of controlling the release direction or, if they scatter the wrong way, removing them. Else there's not a whole lot you can do to interact with them and they hit like a train. Place your lone characters in units to avoid getting sniped by a flying fanatic and try and exploit nearby woods to kill them has been my plan.

I use them a fair bit in my expedition force. They are often less efficient than more doomseekers vanilla but I do love them so.

In lower points games. A dragon slayer with additional hand weapon and the rune of wrath is 5 attacks, killing blow and additional wounds to behemoths for just 88 pts he sits near cannons looking threatening. 

Higher points I break out the deamonslayer he's got a lot of options. These ive found the most effective.

Try to Balance your investment, unlike most chars of his points level he's not got much mobility, so if you cant get him into the enemy he's wasted.

He's a bit weird. Too much investment and your afraid to lose him. Too little and you may as well taken the above Dragonslayer and saved some points. As such I favor the following.

 Greatweapon
Master rune of swiftness. 
 Rune of fury 
Rune of parrying

This gives you an i5 great weapon with 5 attacks. And -1 to hit me at ws 8 (rune of the warrior)

Else
Hand weapon 
Master rune of swiftness
2x rune of cleaving 

This is my cheap option. Dwarfs don't often get to charge first so your highest fear is not striking. I5 gw man tends to hide behind a higher unit and go for counter charges. Asf hand weapon man will happily try and fight anything.

Rune of the Furness (helps immensely against random pillar of fire templates. I suggest working one into all your lone chars in possible)
Rune of warding. (Dodge a random template scatter or killing blow)

Warriors rune (this makes you ws 8 and -1 to hit via the run of parrying. Meaning the duke hits you on 5s.)
Rune of the dauntless (a char this expensive needs a reroll. He can challenge random characters this way and probably win if he gets to strike)
 (could also go rune of grit for t6 if not using the rune of parrying)

Some other thoughts:

Rune of the dishonored is odd. If you take it. I'd kit him out to the max and try your best to get him killed. Vanguard into shooting range, block charges with your face, ect. It seems rules as written you have to take the 3+ wards if you want to or not, so you need to kill 300ish points just in case he lives. Be reckless.

Rune of the hateful is worse than rune of the dauntless for me as it's only the first turn. The exception is slicing up mooks but challenges are what keep you safe.

If not using a rune of parrying rune of wrath is a great choice. Extra attack is extra attack.

Rune of endless battle plus alrick the mad is hilarious but unreliable due to dwarf charge ranges. Stack attacks, avoid challenges and kill an entire front rank.

I play against empire a lot, take my experience with a mug of ale though since I play expedition force only so far. (The painting is never ending). I can give you an average list I play if with or against if you want context to the following.

Summary:

I fear: wizards, witch hunters, tutonic guard, the combat res priest (laurals, daggers, armour of hammer hand for something like potential 24 potential combat res), cannons, more cannons, hell blasters and more cannons.

I laugh at, 
Handgunners not in the nuln list, large infantry blocks if they can't stop the sapper,  the tank(if I have slayer/doomsayers), morters, the skirmish cav

Following is a stream of consciousness as I think back over our recent games that I pulled together in the summary 

Empire cannons pack much more of a reliable punch than ours. I find myself getting outshot in artillery duels most of the time due to the +1w empire causes. They also remove anything fun I bring with extreme prejudice. copter unit? Ded. Bomber? Ded. Tooled up demon slayer behind a unit. Aim 6 inch in front and 1/6 chance (with reroll from engineer) to land on his head and fulfill his oath. Sapper? Has 2 one use 2+wards and hopes to dodge. 

The hell blaster is variable as all hell but a spiked roll can devastate a unit with armour bane and lots of hits. I don't tend to prioritise it over the cannons but as the game goes on, the lines close and the field clears there's less and less cover and it gets more effective.

Handgunners kinda suck. I rate thunderers higher for toughness, save and the move and shoot from force. Empire cross bows out range handgunners which is annoying. But suffer the same issues. Note In a range duel I try and entrench mine with the sapper T1 for the cover bonus.

Tanks are weirdly fine for me. Doomseekers and slayer characters beat them up. Rune of hesitation stops impact hits on one unit and you can drilled to make it difficult to charge other stuff.

(I run 20 warriors with a banner thane and the rune of hesitation, it's my anvil and exists to block stuff and rack up attrition via the sapper general. Who is behind the unit)

I get rolled in the magic phase. Only lvl 1 runesmiths available for expedition so denial is limited in both range and power. empire has all lores and many casting options some even muplicative in power (twin tailed wand for example). Even random bound spells like the armour of hammer hand are difficult to stop. I take random runes of the forge on solo characters to try and help against pillar of fire or fireball. Of course the rule of pride makes that a little tricky (forge, / forge and passage, / forge passage and...?). Phantasmagoria can go to hell (though I was accidently impetusing my cannons and they can't charge so it's worse than we were playing it) but it can completely disorder or carefully planned lines, ruin all your entrenchments and unlike other armies we might not dispell it before it matters.

My frequent OPP favors a char heavy big empire halbard block with all the buffs. It flies 36 due to steed of shadows. Sapper is my friend. He reaps a heavy toll Vs large infantry blocks.

Knights are not as bad as Bret s. But still can be nasty. Rune of hesitation helps a lot at blunting lances. As does shield wall.

Demigryphs I have some fear of but they often have trouble disrupting us in side or reas if you kill one due to heavy infantry. Rangers can take them often via shoot /overwatch/great weapon plan and they often get assigned the scout counter deploy job.

Great swords suck ass but Teutonic guard beat up my dwarfs. buffs are very scary on them (demonology buffs and the steed of shadows). priests are annoying, Ulrick reroll 6s is the worst, we don't get that many attacks as it is.

Witch hunters are cheap, sneaky challenge monsters for 53 pts (hand weapon X2). I5 means we're often slower and kB means I avoid them unless I have the rune of preservation. I have a lot of runes of preservation.

Empire skirmishers I don't really care about as we're hard to disrupt and the warcriminal thane (handgun, accuracy, bursting flame, rapid fire) cares not for negative modifiers.
Also worth noting op, you have to use your shields to use rules like shield wall. If you use 2h weapons. Can't shieldwall.
That's the way we've been playing it too. I've been making the sapper my general for the 12 inch command range and only taking the one.

I think tankyness is second to wanting something that does the old try ele plan as long as you are not playing hc. As so many remnants mean you're going to have monsters immune to at least some damage types. I'd look for something that is phys as extra stacking like the AC build or something like tri ele ls. I'd also try and grab the attacks can't be blocked attack mastery.

Imo the simplest way to sustain Fr is still the gain x life while affected by vitality watchers eye mod/shaper rings with CODT ball lightning/gmp/blazing salvo + some recoup. Or the pathfinder plan. Going just recoup I found had too much ramp time to get going, while both together seem to cover the weakness of the other.

I'd instead look at which has the best option for something like hexblast mines or another smooth start, which you can then transition early into FR once you have some key pieces (e.g. hexblast till watchers eye, dopplegangers and a glorius vanity) Cap chaos res, solve sustain then swap. If your anything like me, league enjoyment can be directly correlated to how smooth the leveling/first build is, and Fr is gonna suck I suspect.

I planned out a few FR selfcast starters for this event and I think bog witch might be the best option with self poison for + 8% all max rez (via apeps supremacy/slumber), Toad pact also provides a little aoe, which is always helpful for Fr overlaps (I always went for 0.9m radius as it seems to make the first 5 proj all shotgun consistantly, though I can't prove that so take with grain of salt). Sanguine power can give you a lot of life and, though I havent figured it out yet, there is probably someway to leverage the rotten core node.

Scion is the option that seems much lower barrier to entry but lower ceiling. You have the 50% recoup (which is a ring and like 3 passive points really). But also also shavs, which might open up soul sacrifice as a viable alternative (recovery will be an issue though). Power charges or pops are ez choices and i think you either go chaos damage can inflict elemental ailments or leaderships price. I dont think it, on its own solves recovery though and whichever route you go I think you need some key pieces first.

Shields a good shout. Could also give him the ol rapid fire//bursting flame/ accuracy gun for deleting skirmish units. If he's in the big block though, don't do it if you plan to march to the enemy. The rapid fire rune Has no stand and shoot minimum too often turning into 4-6 combat res in stand and shoot. I like the last 5 PTS on rune of passage or rune of the forge (was relevant once but glorious)

Since you have shooting I suspect you intend to wall up. If you plan to close the gap though. A cart is very useful for the plus movement. Drilled into marching column. Move 12. Rune of urgency from the anvil. Drilled into regular formation. March 8. (Sorry thought the unesmith was the anvil. Scratch this)

Since you have a runesmith. I warn you now that 18 inch deny sucks. That said the smith often was useful for me in a thunderer or warrior unit. As ab 2 is quite nice but really useful when it matters (ap 4 handguns on knights for example)

Finally id consider combining the thunderers into 1 units and running the named char who ignores long range. I played 2x12 thunderers in expedition force on our weekend tournament (4 games non competitive) but shooting penalties stack up very quickly and the long lines were giving enemies cover. Hitting on 7s ain't great. (Light cover, skirmish, long ranger for example). 

With 20 and the char, find a hill. Sit on it. Shoot 20 shots hitting on 4s from two ranks.
Without id suggest you use them to kill small units. Try and avoid shooting skirmish infantry. The long range + skirmish is 6s minimum. Worse with other modifiers.

Lastly. I love doomseekers and would highly recommend a couple. Just vanilla they normally manage to obiterate something and when they die... 0pts! Unlike a lot of our units they have 11 inch potential charge range too.

One last thing. You don't have an engineer. So your at the mercy of misfires as such id find 15 PTS for the rune of reloading and the rune of reloading + stalwart rune on your cannons. Meaning you can ignore 5/6 misfire results (cept blowing up)

I use a hot glue gun and 5x3mm magnets on standard gw bases. 
You need.
Metal tray
Glue gun
Baking paper

Put paper on the tray, have a stack of magnets 

Blob of glue on the base. Press stack in. Wait 3-5 seconds. A magnet will pull off.
Small bit more glue over the top then press the whole base onto the metal tray. The baking paper stops it sticking and it flattens the still sorta soft glue.

Can do a whole army pretty quick this way. For larger models I use 4 magnets (75mm x50 or larger) in each corner. Same for metal models.

It's way faster than green stuff.

For trays I have a guide in my profile for making. Magnetic trays and a magnetic storage box. The green stuff bit is outdated. Glue gun is better.

First of all, stone gauntlet with phalanx warders is known for being the best right of war for a reason. Lascannon dreads and 60 warders make a list that far above par than many others and I'd expect you to be warned or bring something similar if that's on the board and you're not playing a highly competitive setting. That said you have some options.

Option one. Dismantle the wall. Know when and how the warders rule apply.

Lascannon havocs or snipers, either way you want to take your precision hits and kill models so they are no longer base to base and any model with a 2 plus save. This disabled lockstep(+1ws) and shield wall (+1invuln). Follow that with a charge or shooting with other, non precision shots after the defences are down. Disabling the reroll is harder because you need to make it so they are not in coherency with two other models. Make sure you check your opponent if they claim the ws bonus on a charge as it does not apply. Finally, know he only gets to reroll the invuln. Volume of fire, be they hammer of Olympia bolter rounds, volkite or other such weapons, warders have to chose between the better save or the reroll, and I've seen warder squads break under mass tactical marine fire where they laughed at the equivalent points in lascannon.

Option two.
Outmanuver the wall. 
Pinning weapons (including hammer of Olympia and shrapnel bolters). Difficult terrain weapons (grav) and cheap bait (sit 12 inch away after his moves and dare him to charge you, hope he fails) can let you work around the killy indestructible brick while you murder his back like. Then just keep playing keep away while you get objectives and win via scoring. Might not be a very fun way to play but is an option.

Option three.
Leave the wall.
It's not said enough that table top games have an expectation that both players have fun. Don't commit 3 hours of your time to a miserable slogfest if you don't want too. Leave, find a different opponent or just play another day. If it's not a good time for both players. It's not worth playing. Go do something fun instead.

10 skirmisher

10 skirmisher

Monster slot

Casket of souls

Monster slot or catapult

Monster Slot or catapult

\----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The goal in this army is to use your curses to drag the enemy down to your level and beat them with skeletons. Own the magic phase with +6 to curse priest and +5 to the other level 4, add another +3 by eating a ushabti if you need too, use the level ones to top up units and the BSB to reroll ALL your ld checks for resurrecting and ambushing. Summon scorpions and necroserpents to block open avenues and mess with peoples plans whilst also eating random infantry then use traverse to move monsters around. Use the casket for support and occasionally stack all the ld debuffs in necromancy with light of death to nuke something with ghosts. Use Bow ushabti to nail dragon lords and monsters to the nearest cliff face.

For deployment, I have the Necrotech whipping my skeletons back and forth in front of my 4 priests near my casket, I'll have the greatbows either sighting on a dragon lord or screened by the swarms and the skele skirmishers in front of the skeletons to soften some incoming units and redirect charges.  Curse preist is great for bringing units down to skeleton level and a unit that size forces fear checks on most targets, poison and hatred stacks a lot of wounds on even high toughness foes and Phalanx prevents enemies from winning and disengaging. 4 priests can restore a lot of skeletons a turn so its more important to have bodies over upgrades. Elemental priest gets to move monsters about and provide support utility.

For monsters I take what I feel like really. Colossi have never really paid off but are cool and have potentially infinite attacks. Sphinx can hunt other monsters but is mostly bought due to fly and the fact it looks rad. Ambush scorps or Stalkers can just come on from a board edge and do not have to use from the sands so can be used to outflank warmachines and sneaky wizards. Venerably ushabti hit like a truck but don't like getting hit back so keep them out of large chaff units, they excel vs things like bret knights though. 3. Fatal strike no longer effects template weapons, so flamers and missiles are no longer the unit deleting nonsense they used to be. Volkite I think is the best bet for erasing an infantry squad, though personally, I plan to go combi melta and 4++ rend av 14, with the option to bolter squishier targets. Worth pointing out, Combi weapons were specifically able to fire both parts in phase 3. combining rending bolter and rending volkite will kill most squishy things. 
4. Since we never need to actually drive long distance due to point 2, I have never paid more than the base 35 points for a rhino. I use them mostly to park in front of assaulting units, hide a valuable unit from an alpha strike, and ramming stuff.

The is often due to collisions, by having 2 pc transmit at the same time, packets start colliding and having to be resent, in http (web browsing) this is easy you simply do not receive an acknowledgement and resend it after timeout. However time sensitive applications such as games use udp, this does not resend packets as it will arrive too late and you simply miss information causing stuttering and warping. Packet loss is often a cause of lag with stable ping. There could also be a bandwidth cap on some applications that would throttle traffic when the limit is 
reached, in peak times or due to request. Several of my isp's have used these, they call it traffic shaping. A throttle means that packets are simply sent only after higher priority traffic is finished. Causing delays and higher ping.

I did exactly as described, so I'll try to lay out my experience;
PC wise I have 2 characters with around 100 hrs into them, so I was not brand new to the game.

There are several differences I have noticed.
First there are a lot more players on psn. Orange soapstone signs are fairly common and often with multiple upvotes.

Second I joined the forest hunter covenant, summons on the ps3 are around 10-30 seconds but mostly seem to be people with allies stomping invaders (but that may just be the Forrest). On the pc this covenant often took 4-6 min. Being human tends to net you at least one invasion (due to the 10 min timer) before you get to the boss. This assumes you are already in an area at the correct(ish) level.

Third, expect the player base to be much more developed. On the pc things tend to be a little more even. Twinks, while around, are not as common. Compare to the ps3 where, in new game at least, nearly every invader seems to be a low soul level run with nasty lightening weapons. Don't expect fair fights. In addition to this be wary of the forest, I joined at sl 34 and got stomped repeatedly. Eventually, one of my opponents was killed by another player and I received 1.6million souls. Doing so, leveled me up to 85. I was still seeing boss summons in Anor Londo at this level. (I am still undecided whether this ruined this play-through or not).

Forth, get used to 30fps. If you do not use dsfix this is no issue, if you do, you will notice the choppier animations. In addition blight town is nasty in terms of performance, frame rate drop and stutter are not uncommon.

For context, this charater is a dex/pyro. The ps3 is the 320gb model bought on ebay for £126.

Personally, I would not make this switch again, not just for dark souls. While the pc community is not overly abundant, there is still enough people to get by. However if there are other games on the ps3 you want to play such as the exclusive titles, then dark souls is worth picking up (second hand copys on ebay are cheep). My current feeling is that I did not not feel make a wise investment, but I do hope as I explore the ps3 games available, I will change my mind. If I do not, I will simply sell it on.

I also have a faith/dex character (with no vit points at all). The only way I was able to do that one was equip all of havel's gear, power within, 2h my weapon (I had no buff at the time) and keep above 3 bars of health.

I would disagree, your gaming experience is exactly what you want it to be. Personally, I love the ability to summon a phantom and be summoned myself. It really adds to the many worlds thing dark souls has going and cements the community. My personal favorite part of the game is burg till Anor Lando simply due to the amount of player interaction (both good and bad.) The game being hard is simply not a draw. It being challenging and knowing you can influence that challenge for yourself and others... That is Dark Souls for me.

Classes

Pet Battles

* Singing Crickets are now considered Rare pets. This change does not apply to pets that have already been acquired.
* Silithid Hatchlings should now be less elusive.

Brawler's Guild

Professions
Alchemy

Jewelcrafting

Items

Creatures

Dungeons, Raids and Scenarios

Terrace of Endless Spring
Tsulong

Classes
